changelog: - **A document can declare its resource kinds and ask the engine to keep one of them balanced.** When a graph names resource types on its Pools, a Kinds panel appears above the Inspector with one row per kind: tick Conserved and every Converter that touches that kind must put out exactly what it takes in, rate for rate, with an optional base unit shown as a label. A kind you do not tick is consumed and produced freely, as every model was until now, so nothing changes for the bundled examples or for a document that declares nothing. Each connection has one kind: its Pool's, or on a line with no Pool, the type written on the line itself, carried through Gates. Where a conserved kind is involved, the panel and the selected node's Inspector list what is wrong and the run does not start: a connection joining two kinds, a Gate carrying two, a Converter whose balance differs or cannot be computed because a rate is not a number or a line has no kind. A refused document is still edited, saved and shared as usual. After a step the panel also lists the boundary outflow by kind: what left through each Drain or End, so an evaporation line reads as water into evaporation and never as a nameless loss. A document with a kinds table is saved as `loop-studio/graph/3` (revision note `loop-model/3`); an older version of the app does not open it, and inserting such a structure into a document asks before promoting it. The panel and its findings are in all 18 languages.
